header.label: OpenAEC Foundation
header.title: Get started
header.desc: Start with the OpenAEC ecosystem in 5 steps. No registration, no credit card, no vendor lock-in — just download and get going.

step1.title: Pick the tool that fits your work
step1.desc: Explore the complete ecosystem and pick the tool for your task. For PDF annotation and CAD markup: Open PDF Studio. For 2D CAD drawing: Open 2D Studio. For heat-loss calculations per NEN 12831 and ISSO 51:2023: Open Heatloss Studio. For IFC model validation: BIM Validator. For BCF issue management: BCF Manager Studio. For cost estimation: Open Calc Studio.

step2.title: Download the installer or try the live demo
step2.desc: Every product page offers downloads for Windows (.exe or MSI), macOS (.dmg), Linux (.deb, .AppImage, .snap, .rpm) and Android (.apk). Or click "Live demo" to start straight in your browser — no installation needed.

step3.title: Install and launch the tool
step3.desc: OpenAEC tools are lightweight (8–20 MB) thanks to Tauri 2 + Rust — much smaller than Electron apps. On Windows you can choose between System install (all users, admin required) or User install (no admin needed). On macOS, drag the app into Applications. On Linux, double-click the .deb or .AppImage. No account required to start.
step3.link: Read more about the technical architecture →

step4.title: Work with IFC or import existing data
step4.desc: All OpenAEC tools communicate via IFCX, an open extension of IFC that also supports namespaces for calculations, reports and metadata. Import IFC 2x3, IFC 4 and IFC 4.3 models — including civil schemas like IfcRoad, IfcRail, IfcBridge, IfcTunnel and IfcMarineFacility. Data flows seamlessly between all tools.
step4.link: More on IFCX and civil schemas →

step5.title: Send feedback or contribute
step5.desc: File bugs and feature requests via GitHub (github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation). Join the WhatsApp community or email info@open-aec.com. For companies: request a quote for consultancy, managed hosting or custom extensions. All tools are LGPL-3.0 — fork, modify, contribute.
